reviews.review: Nothings but heresy, the Emperor will hear about this.

"Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine". The game where you're supposed to be the best of the best. One of the strongest thing in the Imperium of Man, however. That is not the case. I bought this game on release a few years ago when it was released and stopped at just at the beginning of Chapter 3. But as the years passed. I couldn't exactly remember why I put down the game, I saw it in my library and figured I'd reinstall it. I couldn't phantom why I put the game down without finishing it. So I booted up Singleplayer again to finish my campaign. 


 I recall watching an interview for the game before its release. I remember them saying, "You're a Space Marine. Cover is for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Space Marine is designed to keep you in the fight." They completely failed on this. The combat is awful. You aren't a Space Marine, you're a ♥♥♥♥♥. Your shields go down in an instant until you get the Iron Halo (which is at the end of the game). You can be torn to shred by Orks no problem. Even the standard Chaos Space Marines you encounter later on the game are tougher than you are.


 Combat is flawed from the very beginning. Since you aren't supposed to be in cover, you're getting shot all the time. No matter where you are. There is no rest in a fight. You're always being hit unless you retreat back and hide behind some crates. Even then, most of the enemies. including the orks have unnatural accuracy. You'll learn to despise the Orks with Rokkit Launchas and Chaos Marines with Plasma Cannons, as they'll volley over any cover you're hiding behind and hit you directly. But then, it doesn't matter. Since the game doesn't focus around cover, you'll still take damage from any rockets or grenades that explode on the other side of what you're hiding behind. One hit is enough to completely remove your shield, and two or three more will outright kill you. So if you get hit by all three rokkits at once? You're dead.


 The game largely revolves around staying in melee combat and preforming executions to keep yourself going. However, if you try to preform one while in the middle of combat, you'll either get the same amount of health you started with, or you'll just die. As I mentioned, enemies have an unnatural accuracy with all their weapon. During the cut scenes for the executions, you can (and will) still get hit by any ranged or unit within melee range. The unnatural accuracy also extends to the point where they can fire through their teammates and still hit you without killing their buddies. (Excluding Grenades and Rokkit Launchas). Later on in the game you'll start encountering chaos pyskers, they'll fire a beam at you and if you're hit in the open by one. You're as good as dead. 


 Fights are all designed around this type of encounter. An extremely powerful ranged unit in the back (or several). While you get swarmed by melee infantry which can quickly over run you. So most of the game is just back peddling into corners to deal with all the melee infantry before you can peek out and take a few pot shots at the ranged units, as staying out for more than a few shots will generally get you killed. This if course, gets worse along in the game as you go from dealing with Orks to Chaos. At some points you'll be getting bombarded by plasma weapons, pyskers and swarmed by traitor guards and regular chaos space marines. Most of those fights require simply dumb luck and very slow movements to progress through. Dealing with Chaos is simply a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, as when you're distracted with those who pose a threat, you'll be getting shot by traitor guard, who serve no purpose other than to take up half of your screen with the hit indicator. 


 So the game is about 6-8 hours of the same combat over and over, ontop of artificial difficulty. It quickly gets frustrating as the game has no actual save system, just check points. Which is extremely annoying as dying some times will put you back right before a lengthy cut scene. (Looking at you, boss fights). Which are unskippable. The game is the same story as literally every other Warhammer game. You're under attack by orks, then SURPRISE ITS CHAOS, even though it was completely obvious from the beginning. 

 Even the very end wave fight is awful, and insanely harder than the last boss.It consist of going through several waves of enemies with little to no cover. Each wave having more ♥♥♥♥ tacked onto it. If you fail it, you have to start back down the hallway so you have to run back and watch the same few minute long cutscene again. The Boss fight after it is a compete joke, its an on-rails quick time event where you fall down a spire. A few moments have free movement where you can dodge stuff thrown at you. For some reason you can fire, but Titus just holds his gun to the side and all the bullets fly off the screen. 

 The secret to killing the boss is this:

 1-1-1, hit space, 1-1-1, hit space. Hit F, cutscene. Repeat x2-3 times.

 Congrats, you win.

TL:DR?

- You play as a weak ass Space Marine Captain.
- Muh Ultrasmurfs.
- Awful, repetitive combat.
- Extremely accurate orcs.
- Demons are somehow weaker than Chaos Marines.
- Same exact story as any of the other games.
- Bad check point system.
- Dead Multiplayer.


 If you're a 40k fan, you'll find several annoying flaws in the game. So I'd recommend passing this game up and go play Dawn of War or Chaos Gate. Something else worth your time.

 If you're looking to have some fun and don't care about repetitive combat. Pick it up for when its less than 20 on a steam sale, forget about all the DLC since mutliplayer is dead.

If you're looking to just play Multiplayer. Don't. The only active game mode is Exterminatus, all of the others are dead. Including the DLC ones, even Chaos Exterminatus. So save yourself the money.

Amazing Storyline,gameplay and bolters...
My God those Bolters sound and 'feel' good.

The multiplayer though.....well since you usually have 1 server running and the players are arond lv40 with most weapon unlocks and add ons, a new player could (and does) feel intimidated up to the point that the dude with the Lascannon gets him from across the map.

In summary- great campaign- unbalanced Multiplayer as only well seasoned plyers really play it
